dish: Hakka abacus seeds (suan pan zi), yam ring & poon choi
address: 16 Jalan Leban, Singapore 577554
w: Widely called Singapore's oldest Hakka restaurant (going back to 1960s Chin Swee Road, at Jalan Leban on the Sembawang Hills/AMK fringe for over 30 years) — the abacus seeds are pounded with more yam than flour and wok-fried with dried shrimp, minced pork and mushroom, alongside stuffed beancurd, khong bak and festive poon choi.

dish: Yong tau foo with a prized house sauce (chee cheong fun option)
n: Xi Xiang Feng Yong Tau Foo
address: Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, #01-23, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724
w: Reliably the longest queue at 724 AMK Central — a half-hour wait even off-peak — for a yong tau foo rated among the island's best, its handmade pieces defined by a deeply savoury house sauce; order it over chee cheong fun (S$0.80) or as laksa (S$3). Widely reviewed by ieatishootipost, Miss Tam Chiak, Eatbook and Seth Lui.

dish: Sliced fish soup with tee po & tomato (30-min queue)
address: 409 AMK Market & Food Centre, #01-15, Blk 409 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560409
w: A two-brother sliced-fish soup stall at 409 (Teck Ghee Square) whose broth balances savoury, sweet and a tang from fresh tomato, layered with tee po (dried sole), soy beans, tofu and seaweed. The queue runs 30 minutes even off-peak; soup from S$5.50, +S$0.50 with bee hoon.

dish: Charcoal & S'mores waffles with soft serve
address: Blk 529 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, #01-2353, S560529
w: The heartland flagship of the North Bridge Road dessert cafe, doing waffle-and-ice-cream sets in an AMK void deck — the charcoal waffle with salted-egg drizzle (S$8.50), an AMK-exclusive 'Yuan Yang' half-charcoal-half-Belgian waffle, and a toasted-marshmallow S'mores waffle (S$15). Open late on weekends.

dish: Light, ghee-fried prata & R.K. Special (60+ flavours)
address: 136-138 Casuarina Road, Singapore 579526
w: One of Singapore's most famous prata houses, on the Casuarina Road / Lower Peirce fringe of AMK — light, ghee-fragrant prata across 60-plus flavours (from Alfredo to salted-egg prawn), plus fish head curry, biryani, thosai and the off-menu R.K. Special (prata in mutton curry with soft-boiled eggs). Open till late.

dish: Handmade fishball mee pok (sister branch of the original)
address: Cheng San Market & Cooked Food Centre, #01-123, Blk 527 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560527
w: Opened by one of the sisters from the original Song Kee, this Cheng San branch draws long queues (fishballs can sell out by 1pm) for honest handmade fishballs — bouncy, not over-salted — with an enhanced fishball and beancurd skin in each bowl. Closed Mondays.

dish: Thai-style wanton mee with springy egg noodles & pork lard
address: Blk 151 Ang Mo Kio Ave 5, #01-05, S560151
w: A long-running Kebun Bahru stall plating Thai-style wanton noodles — al dente egg noodles lightly coated in shallot oil, springy and eggy, with fried wanton, flavourful char siew and crisp pork lard. A dish rarely found outside Thailand and a longtime AMK draw.

dish: Park-side brunch — truffle egg cocotte & crispy fish burger
address: Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park, 510 Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, Singapore 569983
w: A family-friendly bistro set midway through Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park with an alfresco deck over the greenery — Asian-twist brunch of har cheong gai and waffles, truffled egg cocotte, mentaiko fries and a sustainable-fish crispy burger, with craft brews. Around S$22/pax; go early before the queue.

dish: Saigon banh mi & iced salted coffee
address: Blk 260 Ang Mo Kio Street 21, #01-04, S560260
w: A hidden Vietnamese nook in a new AMK BTO estate — a crunchy, well-stuffed Saigon banh mi (S$6.90) with pork floss and meats, plus a milky, subtly savoury ice salted coffee (S$4.90). Small, cash-and-carry, and a genuine rarity in the heartland.

dish: Hainanese-Western chicken cutlet, pork chop & fish & chips
address: Blk 347 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, #01-2142, S560347
w: An old-school hawker-Western institution first opened in 1994 (originally at Blk 711 Ave 8) that reappeared at Blk 347 in 2021 to steady queues — thin, crispy chicken cutlet, pork chop, fish and chips and sirloin steak at heartland prices, in the Hainanese-Western tradition. Closed Wednesdays.

dish: Prawn mee & fried Hokkien mee run by three sisters
address: Mayflower Market & Food Centre, #01-06, Blk 162 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560162
w: A humble Mayflower stall run by three sisters, doing a comforting prawn mee alongside fried Hokkien mee at value prices with generous prawns — friendly service and moderate waits. Opens from 6am; closed Wednesdays.

dish: Poached Hainanese chicken rice (est. 1992)
address: Cheng San Market & Cooked Food Centre, #01-110, Blk 527 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560527
w: Founded in 1992 and run by a father and his two sons, this perpetually-queued Cheng San stall poaches its chicken the traditional way — an ice bath sets the gelatin under the skin for a slippery, slightly fatty finish — and debones it for you. Plates around S$4.50.

dish: Handmade sheng mian & mee hoon kueh in pork-ikan bilis broth
n: Seletar Sheng Mian & Mian Fen Guo
address: Kebun Baru Market & Food Centre, #01-07, Blk 226H Ang Mo Kio Street 22, S560226
w: A perpetual-queue stall at Kebun Baru for hand-torn mee hoon kueh and hand-pulled sheng mian, the noodles the pride of the house, in a broth boiled with pork bones and ikan bilis for a natural sweetness. Dry or soup, S$4-6.

dish: Pillowy min jiang kueh, cone crepes & putu mayam
address: Teck Ghee Court Market & Food Centre, #01-27, Blk 341 Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, S560341
w: Aunty Belinda's morning stall at Teck Ghee Court is prized for min jiang kueh with a generous filling-to-pancake ratio (peanut, coconut or red bean), a crisp cone-crepe version, and putu mayam (S$1.80 for two). Often sold out before noon.

dish: Charcoal kaya toast (Emperor buns) & sous-vide eggs since 1968
address: Sembawang Hills Food Centre, 590 Upper Thomson Road, S574419
w: A traditional kopi-and-toast stall serving breakfast since 1968, now run by a third-generation mother-and-son duo — award-winning homemade kaya with a strong coconut aroma slathered on soft, crisp-edged 'Emperor' buns, paired with sous-vide eggs and old-school kopi.

dish: Mixed beef laksa (coconut laksa gravy with beef)
n: Hong Heng Beef Noodle Soup & Laksa
address: Kebun Baru Market & Food Centre, #01-16, Blk 226H Ang Mo Kio Street 22, S560226
w: A rare stall selling both beef noodles and laksa under one roof — and, unusually, a Mixed Beef Laksa (S$5.50) that spoons coconut-rich laksa gravy over tender beef. Also a dry beef noodle with thick bee hoon and a fresh-cockles laksa. Relocated to Kebun Baru from AMK Ave 3; closed Mondays.

dish: Fried ice cream & Vietnamese bites in a void deck
address: Ang Mo Kio (void-deck cafe; exact block to confirm at geocode)
w: A cosy void-deck cafe (Fried Ice Cream) that pairs its signature fried ice cream with Vietnamese-leaning bites — an unpretentious neighbourhood dessert-and-coffee spot that made both Eatbook's and HungryGoWhere's Ang Mo Kio round-ups.

dish: Loaded wanton mee with braised chicken feet & pork lard
address: Mayflower Market & Food Centre, Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560162 (stall no. to confirm)
w: A value-for-money wanton mee whose secret is in the lard-based sauce — springy egg noodles loaded with braised chicken feet, char siew and crispy pork lard bits. A long-standing local favourite carried over from its Blk 453 origins.

dish: Tom yum nam kun & claypot tanghoon with prawns
address: Chengsan Centre, #01-2371, Blk 529 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560529
w: A homely Thai stall (also in Toa Payoh) plating authentic street-Thai — a prawn-generous seafood tom yum nam kun (S$6.50), green curry with prawns, papaya salad and a peppery claypot tanghoon with prawns that stays springy. Affordable and consistently recommended.

dish: Neighbourhood specialty coffee & bakes
address: Blk 716 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, #01-4014, S560716
w: A quiet void-deck specialty-coffee cafe on AMK Ave 6 — espresso and pour-overs with cakes and light bites, one of the heartland cafe finds featured in both Daniel Food Diary's and HungryGoWhere's Ang Mo Kio guides.
